newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Poor yields blamed for transatlantic cargo decline.
newsitem.headline: Poor yields blamed for transatlantic cargo decline.

text.p: Poor yields were blamed for the decline in transatlantic freight traffic handled at Brussels airport in 1996, an airport spokesman said.
"Rates across the Atlantic have been particularly low, carriers were perhaps more interested in pushing cargo on the Europe-Asia routes than across the Atlantic."

New York, the airport's number one cargo destination saw a 14.23 percent drop in cargo volumes to 53,062 tonnes in 1996 compared to 1995, and Chicago, its fifth-ranked destination, saw a decline of 24.48 Percent to 12,952 tonnes, an airport statement said.

The spokesman added that it would be interesting to see the results of recent moves by the carriers to increase rates. Currently it was too early to say whether these measures had been effective, he said. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
